summary: Security audit of frontend (bike tab) and environment configuration. No critical vulnerabilities found. Several medium-severity issues identified in credential handling and error reporting.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.description: API credentials (Strava, Intervals.icu) stored in sessionStorage instead of httpOnly/secure cookies. While sessionStorage is ephemeral (cleared on session end), it is accessible to JavaScript and vulnerable to XSS-injected code. Legacy code cleared credentials from localStorage, indicating prior disk-backed persistence.
evidence: Comment: Upload tokens live ONLY in sessionStorage: cleared on session end
vulnerabilities.impact: If XSS vulnerability exists, attacker could steal API tokens and use them to upload malicious activities to user's Strava/Intervals.icu accounts.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Store credentials in httpOnly, Secure cookies instead of sessionStorage. Implement strict CSP to prevent inline scripts.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through Error Message
vulnerabilities.description: API error responses included verbatim in thrown Error messages. Strava or Intervals.icu responses may contain sensitive details (rate-limit headers, internal errors), exposed to console and error logs.
evidence: throw new Error(`intervals.icu upload failed (${res.status}): ${await res.text()}`);
vulnerabilities.impact: Information leakage: error details logged in console, potentially exposed in error reporting services.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return generic error message to client. Log full response server-side only.

vulnerabilities.description: Empty catch blocks in checkpoint() and discard() silently swallow storage errors. If localStorage quota exceeded, ride data loss goes unnoticed.
vulnerabilities.impact: Silent data loss: user may think ride is saved but checkpoint failed; data lost on tab close.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Log errors and emit 'warning' event to view layer to alert user about storage issues.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Calls
vulnerabilities.description: Custom XML parser does not limit recursion depth or entity expansion. Deeply nested ZWO elements or billion-laughs attacks could cause DoS or excessive memory use.
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of Service: malicious ZWO file causes parser to hang or consume excessive memory.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add recursion depth limit (max 100 levels). Disable entity expansion or replace with trusted XML library.

positives: No hardcoded secrets in provided code.
No SQL injection risk (file-based JSON storage only).
XSS mitigated: view.js uses H.escHtml() for all dynamic HTML.
File permissions enforced: env files are 0600 (owner read/write only).
Path traversal defense: Python backend uses resolve() + is_relative_to() + is_file() checks.
not_applicable: SQL Injection: not applicable (JSON file storage, no SQL database).
CSRF: not applicable (no form-based state-changing operations).
Deserialization attacks: JSON.parse() used only on app-managed files.
riskScoreJustification: 38/100 (Low-to-Medium). No critical vulnerabilities (RCE, auth bypass, hardcoded secrets). Identified credential storage concerns (sessionStorage vs httpOnly) and information disclosure in error handling—defense-in-depth improvements, not exploitable flaws.
recommendations: Migrate API token storage from sessionStorage to httpOnly, Secure cookies with server-side token refresh.
Sanitize or suppress API error responses; log full details server-side only, return generic error to client.
Add graceful error handling and user warnings for storage quota errors in recorder.js.
Add recursion depth and entity expansion limits to XML parser in workouts.js, or replace with trusted library.
Add pre-commit hook to reject commits of .env files.
Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) header: script-src 'self', style-src 'self', no inline scripts.
Fuzz XSS: inject script tags into ZWO file names, activity titles, and plan descriptions.
